Transforming IT Support Services to Empower Homeland Security | CACI Overview Remote work, once largely an exception, became the new normal during the COVID-19 pandemic, when the number of people working from home tripled. This work relocation created a seismic shift in technology environments. Engineers and support staff could no longer be at their coworkers’ desks to solve problems, and the volume of technical support tickets and calls rapidly spiked. The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) was no exception during this time. While many employees already were dispersed geographically prior to the pandemic, many more were asked to work remotely to continue their critical work while keeping themselves and their customers safe. When IT issues arose – often at the least expected time – deskside services were no longer an option. DHS was well-equipped to tackle this work environment transformation through CACI’s desk support services, which provide a wide swath of IT capabilities to more than 18,000 employees, primarily those serving DHS headquarters’ mission. “We run the gamut of customer-facing services such as call center, service desk, and field support services all the way up to network engineering, cyber, and cloud services – it’s a broad scope and our technicians and engineers ensure operational excellence at every touchpoint possible,” said Jhon Pak, CACI program manager. “No matter the time or location, we meet the DHS national security mission by providing support services for all their technologies.” 18,000+ users 150,000 service desk calls annually 240 locations g

ction in emails 73% increase in problem resolution ## More than a service desk The DSS program has far outgrown its service desk scope, now supporting software development, network engineering, systems engineering, cloud migration, and cybersecurity. “We can do anything the government dreams of. The only requirement we have now is what the stakeholders want. It’s quite expansive compared to its humble beginnings,” Pak said. Post-pandemic, hybrid and remote work remain commonplace, and as such, other agencies look to DSS 2.0 as a model of developing trust with end users to execute flexible, scalable, modern support services. “End users want to feel confident they can do their jobs without a technician figuratively on standby for whenever they need to do basic troubleshooting,” Pak said. “That confidence then provides our experts the capacity to tackle the complex problems only they can solve.”

Job ID 324320 The Opportunity: Join our innovative team as a Senior Technologist in a role that sits at the intersection of legacy mainframe systems and cutting-edge AI technology. This position offers a unique opportunity to serve as the critical technical bridge between modern systems engineering and mainframe operations while integrating emerging AI capabilities into legacy development workflows. You'll lead efforts to incorporate emerging AI technologies into the mission space, translate those capabilities into practical tools for mainframe developers, and maintain mission-critical COBOL-based financial management systems running on z/OS. This role provides exceptional growth potential as you'll not only support current infrastructure but also shape the modernization strategy and technology roadmap for legacy system transformation while working with a diverse team of infrastructure engineers and mainframe developers. What You'll Be Working On The system is a large-scale COBOL application processing financial management data for a federal client. It runs nightly batch cycles on z/OS, uses Db2 and VSAM for data storage, and includes a C/C++ GUI communicating with the mainframe via TCP/IP and CICS. In parallel, the team is deploying a private, secure LLM instance to assist with development tasks—code explanation, documentation, query generation, and more. Thi

s role sits at the center of both efforts: keeping the legacy system stable, advancing the modernization agenda, and building the bridge between the team's mainframe expertise and its emerging AI capabilities. Responsibilities: Primary: Systems Engineering & Modernization Lead technical discussions on migration strategy, evaluating pathways to modernize legacy workflows and components over time Support Development and maintenance of C/C++ components, including GUI and interface layers that communicate with the mainframe application via TCP/IP and CICS Drive adoption of VS Code and modern developer tooling across the team, including mainframe-facing extensions such as IBM Z Open Editor. Design, implement, and maintain CI/CD pipelines accommodating both modern and mainframe build, test, and deployment orchestration using industry DevOps & CI/CD tooling such as GitLab or equivalent tooling Manage the code repository, including branching strategies, merge request workflows, access controls, and integration with mainframe source control tools Secondary: Technical Liaison Serve as the primary point of coordination between system engineers and the mainframe development team, translating requirements, capabilities, and constraints in both directions Lead the adoption of emerging AI tools for team use, working alongside system engineers on deployment configuration, access controls, and operational parameters. (NYSE: CACI) today announced the launch of Good Dogs for Great Americans, the company's signature philanthropy program dedicated to helping veterans regain independence through specially trained service dogs. In partnership with the Washington Capitals and America's VetDogs, the program turns defense on the ice into life-changing support for those who defended our nation. Continue Reading View File Download File Heroes come in pairs: Service dogs offer independence and support for those who served. View File Download File Bravo reporting for duty! He's the very first pup sponsored by Good Dogs for Great Americans. As the ambassador for Good Dogs for Great Americans, Lt. Gen. (Ret.) Mike Shields, CACI Senior Vice President, brings more than three decades of Army leadership and a commitment to serving America's veterans. "Throughout my Army career, I learned that no one succeeds alone. We rely on trusted teammates to overcome obstacles and accomplish the mission," said Shields. "For many veterans, a specially trained service dog becomes that trusted partner. The dogs provide greater independence, renewed confidence, reduced anxiety, and unwavering support every day. I'm proud to help champion CACI's Good Dogs for Great Americans because this organization allows more veterans the opportunity to experience that profound partnership and improved quality of life." The program comes to life through CACI On Defense, CACI's season-long activation with the Washington Capitals. Throughout the NHL season, CACI will donate $250 to America's VetDogs for every Capitals blocked shot. Those donations will help train and place service dogs with veterans living with physical disabilities, post-traumatic stress, hearing and vision loss, and other challenges. Based on the team's average of approximately 1,300 blocked shots each season, the partnership is expected to fund training for up to eight service dogs annually. Service dogs trained by America's VetDogs help veterans and first responders navigate everyday life, increase mobility, independence, and improve overall well-being. Each placement helps individuals regain confidence while strengthening their connection to their communities. "We are incredibly proud to partner with CACI in support of our mission to provide life-changing service dogs to veterans with disabilities," said John Miller, president and CEO of America's VetDogs. "A service dog can restore confidence, independence and dignity, empowering a veteran to navigate everyday life with greater freedom. CACI's partnership will help us expand that impact and reach more veterans who can benefit from these extraordinary partnerships. We are grateful for their commitment to those who have served and for helping ensure more veterans have access to the support they deserve, at no cost to them." "We're thrilled to partner with CACI through the CACI On Defense Program. CACI has been an outstanding partner to the Capitals, and this platform reflects a shared commitment to honoring and supporting our nation's veterans. It gives us a meaningful way to support the veteran community that means so much to the Capitals and our fans, and we're excited to build on this partnership and create lasting impact for years to come," said Patrick Duffy, Chief Partnership Officer at Monumental Sports & Entertainment. Throughout the season, fans will experience CACI On Defense through in-arena features, broadcast integrations, social media, and community storytelling, highlighting how every blocked shot helps change veterans' lives. About America's VetDogs For more than 20 years, America's VetDogs ( www.VetDogs.org ) has trained and placed guide and service dogs to provide independence, enhanced mobility, and companionship to veterans with disabilities from all eras. In 2015, America's VetDogs opened its programs to first responders, including fire, police, and emergency medical personnel. America's VetDogs is a 501(c)(3) not-for-profit organization founded by the Guide Dog Foundation (est. 1946) and serves our country's and communities' heroes in all 50 states, Washington, DC. Puerto Rico, and beyond. America's VetDogs relies on contributions from generous individuals, corporations, service clubs, and foundations to fund its mission to help those who have served our country live with dignity and independence. It costs more than $50,000 to breed, raise, train, and place one assistance dog, but America's VetDogs provides its services completely free of charge to the individual. America's VetDogs has been accredited by both the International Guide Dog Federation and Assistance Dogs International. Apply, volunteer, and donate at VetDogs.org. verified_source_context.text: CACI Partners with Oracle to Deliver Federal Human Resources IT Modernization to the Office of Personnel Management - Aug 3, 2026 Close Search Search Open Menu Search Close News Releases Event Calendar Close SEC Filings Annual Reports Quarterly Results Financial & Operating Database Close Leadership and Board of Directors Governance Documents ESG Investors Committee Charters Committee Composition CACI Hotline Program & FAQs Close Stock Quote Financial Calculators Historic Price Lookup Close Analyst Coverage Email Alerts Investor FAQs Stock Transfer Agent Info Contact Us News Releases Download PDF Company Release - 08/03/2026 CACI Partners with Oracle to Deliver Federal Human Resources IT Modernization to the Office of Personnel Management RESTON, Va. , Aug. 3, 2026 / PRNewswire / -- CACI International Inc (NYSE: CACI) announced today that it will serve as one of Oracle's technology partners for the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's (OPM) Federal Human Resources Information Technology (HRIT) Modernization contract. Working alongside Oracle, Baker Tilly, and Deloitte on this 10-year contract worth nearly $400 million, CACI will modernize and consolidate disparate federal human resource systems into a single, secure, cloud-based platform for federal civilian employees, including HR professionals and leaders. The consolidation of federal HR systems into a single shared platform is expected to reduce taxpayer costs by more than 90 percent while improving efficiency, security, and service delivery across the government. "Modernizing federal human resources systems at this scale requires trusted technology partners and deep implementation experience," said John Mengucci , CACI President and Chief Executive Officer. " We have already demonstrated that we can deliver complex HR modernization across the federal government. We will apply that experience to help OPM build a secure, modern platform that strengthens data quality, improves the employee experience, and provides the reliability and security federal agencies expect." CACI will support the development, deployment, and implementation of the Oracle Fusion HCM SaaS solution, The platform will include embedded artificial intelligence, standardized data exchange, and continuously updated privacy and security protections. The award builds on CACI and Oracle's proven success delivering large-scale federal HR modernization. Together, the companies supported the Army's Integrated Personnel and Pay System–Army (IPPS-A) , the first successful modernization of the Army's personnel and pay environment after decades of unsuccessful efforts. IPPS-A now supports more than 1.1 million soldiers and established a proven model for transforming complex federal HR systems. The OPM program represents the next step in applying that experience across a large federal HR modernization market. It also expands a long-standing CACI and Oracle partnership that includes work on the Global Combat Support System–Marine Corps (GCSS-MC) platform , the Defense Agencies Initiative (DAI) , and the U.S. Air Force's Defense Enterprise Accounting and Management System (DEAMS) program. About CACI CACI International Inc (NYSE: CACI) is a technology-first national security company that expands the limits of national security through innovation, discipline, and operational excellence. We deliver advanced technologies that help our customers move faster, operate more efficiently, and anticipate and defeat evolving threats. Our 27,000 talented employees and strong culture drive our success and have earned CACI recognition as a Fortune World's Most Admired Company. CACI is a member of the Fortune 500™, the Russell 1000 Index, and the S&P MidCap 400 Index. For more information, visit caci.com. Show all results Posts CACI launches Ask Aida, its AI platform to accelerate data analysis at scale CACI launches Ask Aida, its AI platform to accelerate data analysis at scale Dan Parr 08/06/2026 2 min read Share Share on X Share on LinkedIn Send via email Copy page link In this Article About Ask Aida About CACI CACI is delighted to announce the launch of Ask Aida , its AI platform designed to help businesses analyse CACI’s trusted data rapidly and at scale. Ask Aida brings together CACI’s proprietary data sets and models with customer data, where required, to surface answers instantly. Ask Aida reduces the time taken to analyse data across teams, democratising access to insights and enabling faster answers to everyday business questions. For example, if you need deeper insights into existing and prospective customers for an activity such as a product launch, Ask Aida can provide a comprehensive overview using CACI’s demographic and consumer data. This allows you to quickly understand specific consumer segments and access detailed information across more than 700 attributes, delivering fast, accurate results. Removing the stress from the early stages of decision-making, Ask Aida provides instant overviews that can then be explored in more detail, freeing analysts to focus on ideas that drive tangible business outcomes. To watch this video, please enable Marketing cookies . Manage cookie settings “We’re delighted to be launching Ask Aida,” says Tracy Weir, Chief Executive of CACI. “It provides our clients with a faster, more flexible way to access our market-leading data. We’ve worked closely with our clients to deliver a solution they truly need. Ask Aida provides AI technology in a solution that is compliant with UK legislation, delivering answers that are relevant and secure, based on data from CACI and the data you choose to add into it. “This is a landmark product for CACI, making access to our data easier and more efficient than ever. More people in your organisation will have smart access to interrogate the insight. I’m really excited about the possibilities this opens up.” About Ask Aida Ask Aida is CACI’s agentic AI platform, designed to transform how organisations leverage CACI’s data and models and blend it with their own data. It is more than just an LLM. It understands language as well as the client’s world. It’s a productivity engine that empowers users across an organisation to unlock the full value of their data. It delivers actionable intelligence at scale, securely and ethically, all backed by CACI’s human intelligence. About CACI CACI Ltd is a wholly owned subsidiary of CACI International Inc. Headquartered in London, our operations take place from multiple offices across the UK, Europe and India with over 1650 full-time employees. We empower organisations to make bold, strategic moves with the power of data and technology and our expertise spans industries, from retail and finance to public sector and transport – delivering intelligent solutions that drive progress and create measurable impact.
